result.title: How Reliable Is Visual Token Selection? Rethinking Pruning in Multimodal LLMs
result.comment: Accepted to Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EACL 2027
result.summary: Visual token pruning improves the efficiency of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by removing redundant visual tokens, yet the reliability of existing selection signals has not been systematically examined. We analyze token selection under semantics-preserving perturbations and across representative pruning criteria, revealing two limitations. First, attention-based importance shifts non-uniformly under perturbations, so magnitude alone cannot distinguish stable evidence from unstable saliency (local instability). Second, attention- and diversity-based methods select substantially different subsets despite comparable performance, showing that useful evidence is not confined to a unique subset (global inconsistency). These findings motivate reliable token-set construction. We instantiate this perspective in CoRePruner, a training-free framework combining instruction-aware diversity with reliability-aware attention. Across image benchmarks, multiple MLLM architectures, and token budgets, CoRePruner improves performance, especially under aggressive pruning, and remains competitive on video benchmarks. Our results establish reliability as a central consideration in visual token selection.

AI.brief_summary: 该文系统检验 MLLM 视觉 token 剪枝中「选择信号」的可靠性：在语义保持扰动下发现注意力重要性局部不稳，且不同准则选出的子集差异明显却性能相近，并据此提出免训练的 CoRePruner，将指令感知多样性与可靠性加权注意力结合。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「注意力显著性≠稳定证据」的诊断与「有用证据不唯一」的观察，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选及注意力结构对 latent 内容的影响；但方法面向推理效率，未涉及 latent 推理状态的生成与使用。
